cases.ac: Stone block: clicks 1-2 show crack stages, click 3 removes it and +1 stone inventory; HUD updates.
cases.oracle: Running 'node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern=hard-block-3hits tests/minicraft.logic.test.mjs' passes with zero failing and zero skipped tests: with BLOCKS hardness stone=wood=3 and grass/dirt/leaf=1, dig hit 1 then hit 2 on a stone cell each leave the cell occupied while the per-cell damage map entry increments 1 then 2 and the crack overlay exposes stage hits-1 (visible stage 1, then stage 2, as a pure function of (x, y, stage)); hit 3 removes the block (cell emptied), deletes the damage entry, and increments the stone inventory by exactly 1 so the HUD count updates; a wood cell shows the identical 3-hit behavior; grass/dirt/leaf (hardness 1) never create a damage entry or crack stage.

cases.ac: Grass block: single click removes, +1 grass inventory.
cases.oracle: Running 'node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern=soft-block-single tests/minicraft.logic.test.mjs' passes with zero failing and zero skipped tests: a single dig hit on a grass cell removes the block immediately (no damage-map entry, no crack stage) and increments the grass inventory by exactly 1; dirt and leaf (hardness 1) behave the same; a dig on an already-empty cell is a no-op that changes neither cells nor inventory.

cases.ac: Placing from palette decrements that type's inventory and refuses at 0.
cases.oracle: Running 'node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern=inventory-place-zero tests/minicraft.logic.test.mjs' passes with zero failing and zero skipped tests: placing a block of a selected type decrements that type's inventory by exactly 1 and writes the target cell; when that type's inventory is 0, placement is refused before any mutation — the target cell is unchanged and the inventory stays 0, never negative; after every operation all four counters remain non-negative integers over type keys 1..4.

cases.ac: Reload persists both the world and the inventory (localStorage).
cases.oracle: Running 'node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern=persist-reload tests/minicraft.logic.test.mjs' passes with zero failing and zero skipped tests: saving writes one single localStorage key as an atomic JSON blob {version:2, cells, inventory}; loading that blob restores cells and inventory deep-equal (node:assert deepStrictEqual) to the saved state; with empty/missing storage the game boots with the default world and inventory all-zero {1:0, 2:0, 3:0, 4:0}; a legacy version-1 blob {version:1, cells} migrates with inventory defaulted to zero; the transient damage map does not survive reload.

cleanup.environment: no persistent environment change: each check is a short-lived 'node --test' child process executed from the repo root; no dev server, browser session, global install or daemon is created or left running
cleanup.data: checks only read demos/minicraft/index.html and write nothing into the project; persistence behavior is exercised through an in-memory storage stub or a temp directory, so no real localStorage, no live demo save key and no tracked file is mutated; any test-created temp files under the OS temp dir are removed after the run
